npcs.name: Captain Sterling
npcs.personality: Old-school, stern but fair. The boat comes first, always.

npcs.name: Victoria
npcs.personality: Demanding perfectionist. Tests everyone's loyalty. Former yacht model.

npcs.name: Jade
npcs.personality: Competitive, been angling for promotion. Has history with Derek.

npcs.name: Marco
npcs.personality: Hot-headed Italian. Temperamental genius. Screams in the galley.

npcs.name: Derek
npcs.personality: Laid-back surfer bro. Flirty with everyone. Easy on the eyes.

npcs.name: Connor
npcs.personality: Hard worker, secretly insecure. Quietly observant. Has a crush on you.

npcs.name: Bree
npcs.personality: Party girl. Could be your ally or rival. Knows everyone's secrets.

bd_intro_001.text:
The Mediterranean sun beats down on the marina as your taxi pulls up to the dock. There she is - HMS Longboy, 150 feet of gleaming white luxury. Your stomach does a flip.

This is it. Your first season as a yacht stew. You just got your ENG1 medical certificate three weeks ago, and somehow landed this gig through a friend of a friend.

*Don't screw this up,* you tell yourself.

bd_intro_002.text:
You grab your duffel bag and make your way down the dock. The yacht is enormous - three decks, a hot tub on the sun deck, and what looks like a full bar on the aft.

A woman in a crisp white polo appears at the gangway. Her blonde hair is pulled back impossibly tight, her makeup flawless despite the heat. She looks you up and down with the expression of someone examining a disappointing appetizer.

bd_intro_victoria.speaker: victoria
bd_intro_victoria.text:
"You must be the new third stew. I'm Victoria, Chief Stew. You're late."

You check your phone. You're actually ten minutes early.

"On this boat, early is on time, and on time is late. Remember that."

She turns and walks up the gangway without waiting for you.

bd_intro_003.text:
You follow Victoria into the main salon, trying not to gawk at the crystal chandeliers and marble floors. She rattles off information at machine-gun speed - laundry schedule, turndown service protocols, breakfast mise en place.

You're furiously trying to commit everything to memory when a tanned guy in board shorts wanders through, coffee in hand.

bd_intro_derek.speaker: derek
bd_intro_derek.text:
"Fresh meat!" He grins and gives you an obvious once-over. "I'm Derek, Bosun. If you ever need anything... and I mean *anything*... deck crew's got you."

Victoria rolls her eyes so hard you're surprised they don't get stuck.

"Derek. Don't you have anchor chain to polish?"

"Always so tense, Vic." He winks at you and saunters off toward the bow.

bd_intro_jade.text:
A brunette in a matching white polo appears from below deck. She's pretty, but her smile doesn't quite reach her eyes when she sees you.

"So you're my new shadow. I'm Jade, Second Stew. Victoria put me in charge of training you." She emphasizes 'training' like it's a punishment.

"Just so we're clear - I've been working toward Chief Stew for two years. This is *my* boat. We good?"

bd_intro_response.text: Jade stares at you, waiting for a response. You can already tell she's going to be a problem. How do you handle this?

choices.text: Play it safe - be super agreeable
choices.response_text:
"Totally understood. I'm just here to learn from the best."

Jade's expression softens slightly. She wasn't expecting that.

"Good. At least you know your place."

choices.text: Stand your ground - you're not a pushover
choices.response_text:
"I'm here to work hard and prove myself. But I'm not here to be anyone's doormat."

Jade's eyes narrow. "We'll see about that."

Victoria, overhearing, looks mildly impressed despite herself.

choices.text: Kill her with kindness
choices.response_text:
"Hey, I get it - new people are stressful. But I think we could actually be a great team. Want to grab a drink after the tour?"

Jade blinks, thrown off. "I... maybe. We'll see."

It's not a yes, but it's not a no either.

choices.text: Smile sweetly... while plotting her downfall
choices.response_text:
"Oh, absolutely! I'm just here to support whatever you need. You're clearly *so* good at this."

You smile your most innocent smile - the one you practiced in the mirror. Jade looks satisfied. Pleased, even.

*Enjoy it while it lasts, sweetheart.*

Because here's the thing about girls like Jade - they're so busy watching the door, they never notice the knife sliding between their ribs. You didn't get this job to fold towels and fetch cocktails. You got this job to *win*.

And Jade? She just became the first obstacle.

bd_intro_captain.text:
Before you can dwell on Jade's territorial behavior, heavy footsteps sound from the bridge. A silver-haired man in an immaculate captain's uniform descends the stairs. Everything about him radiates authority - from his weathered tan to his perfectly pressed epaulettes.

The whole crew seems to stand a little straighter.

bd_intro_sterling.speaker: sterling
bd_intro_sterling.text:
"So you're the new stew." Captain Sterling's voice is gravel and sea salt. "Let me make one thing clear: this boat is my home, these guests are my responsibility, and every person on this crew reflects on me personally."

He steps closer, eyes drilling into yours.

"I don't care about drama. I don't care about hookups. I care about excellence. Can you give me that?"

bd_intro_captain_response.text: Captain Sterling waits for your answer. This feels like a test.

choices.text: "Yes, Captain. You have my word."
choices.response_text:
"Good." He nods once, sharply. "Don't make me regret taking a chance on a green stew."

He turns and heads back to the bridge. You exhale slowly.

choices.text: "I'll work harder than anyone, I promise!"
choices.response_text:
Captain Sterling's expression doesn't change. "Promises are easy. Results are what matter."

He heads back to the bridge, leaving you feeling like you said too much.

choices.text: "I'll do my best. I'm still learning, but I'm a fast learner."
choices.response_text:
Something that might be respect flickers in the Captain's eyes. "Honesty. I appreciate that. Most greenies come in here thinking they know everything."

He almost smiles. Almost. "Don't let me down."

bd_intro_crew_meeting.text:
That evening, the full crew gathers in the crew mess for the charter briefing. You finally meet everyone:

*Marco*, the Italian chef, immediately starts complaining about the tiny galley. *Connor*, the lead deckhand, gives you a shy smile and quickly looks away. *Bree*, the other deckhand, studies you with obvious curiosity.

Victoria pulls up the guest preference sheet on her tablet.

bd_charter1_briefing.speaker: victoria
bd_charter1_briefing.text:
"Alright, first charter of the season. Our primary is Chad Worthington III. Crypto millionaire, 28 years old. He's bringing five friends."

She scrolls through the sheet with growing dismay.

"Special requests include... a DJ booth on the sun deck, only Dom Perignon - and I quote - 'none of that poor people champagne,' and... oh for God's sake... a 3am pool party on the first night."

bd_charter1_briefing_2.speaker: marco
bd_charter1_briefing_2.text:
Marco slams his hand on the table. "Madonna! I have to make a tasting menu and they want POOL PARTY at 3am?! When do I sleep?!"

"You don't," Victoria says flatly. "None of us do. Welcome to charter season."

bd_c1_arrival.text:
The next morning, the guests arrive in a fleet of black SUVs. Chad Worthington III steps onto the dock wearing designer sunglasses, a silk shirt unbuttoned to his navel, and an expression that suggests the world is his personal inconvenience.

His entourage - four guys and one woman who appears to be dating all of them simultaneously - spill out behind him.

bd_c1_arrival_2.speaker: sterling
bd_c1_arrival_2.text:
Captain Sterling greets them at the gangway with practiced charm. "Welcome aboard the Longboy, Mr. Worthington. We're honored to have you."

"Chad. Call me Chad." He doesn't shake the Captain's hand, just walks past him. "Where's the champagne? We've been in a car for like, twenty minutes. I'm parched."

bd_c1_champagne.text: Victoria shoots you a look. Champagne service is your job. The Dom is chilled and ready - but you also spot Chad's friend eyeing the cheaper Veuve Clicquot. Do you:

choices.text: Stick to the preference sheet - Dom only
choices.response_text:
You pour six perfect glasses of Dom Perignon. Chad takes one without looking at you.

"Finally. Someone who can read." He sips and nods. "This'll do."

You catch Victoria's approving nod. One small victory.

choices.text: Ask the guests what they'd prefer
choices.response_text:
"We have Dom Perignon as requested, but we also have some excellent—"

Chad cuts you off. "Did I stutter on the preference sheet? Dom. Only. Don't offer me peasant bubbles."

His friends laugh. Your face burns as you pour the Dom in silence.

bd_c1_tour.text:
The boat tour is a disaster. Chad's friends leave champagne glasses everywhere. One of them, a guy named Bryce, spills red wine on the white leather sofa within five minutes. You're on your knees scrubbing the stain when Chad leans over you.

"Hey, new girl. What time's dinner?"

"8pm, Mr. Worth— Chad."

"Make it 10. We're going swimming."

bd_c1_marco_rage.speaker: marco
bd_c1_marco_rage.text:
When you relay the time change to Marco, he nearly throws a pan across the galley.

"TEN?! I have SOUFFLÉ planned! Soufflé does not WAIT! These people... these ANIMALS..."

He launches into a stream of Italian that you're pretty sure includes several curse words and possibly a threat on Chad's life.

bd_c1_dinner_prep.text:
The afternoon passes in a blur of drink requests, sunscreen applications, and watching Derek demonstrate water toys while the female guest films him for her Instagram.

By 9pm, the guests are well on their way to drunk. One of them has passed out on a sun lounger. Chad is playing DJ on his phone, blasting music that makes the crystal rattles.

Dinner service is about to begin.

bd_c1_dinner_service.text:
Marco's seven-course tasting menu is a work of art. The first three courses go smoothly enough - the guests are impressed, even Chad gives a grudging "not bad."

Then, during the lobster course, Bryce turns to you.

"Hey, you. More wine."

He's already slurring. His glass is full. This is his fourth bottle.

bd_c1_wine_choice.text: Bryce is clearly hammered and demanding more wine. His glass is literally full. How do you handle this?

choices.text: Keep pouring - guest is always right
choices.response_text:
You top off his already-full glass, sending wine spilling onto the table cloth. Bryce doesn't notice or care.

"That's more like it."

Thirty minutes later, he vomits on the aft deck. You spend an hour cleaning it up.

choices.text: Suggest water and a palate cleanser
choices.response_text:
"Of course! And may I suggest some sparkling water and a sorbet to cleanse the palate before the next course? It really brings out the wine's full flavor."

Bryce blinks slowly. "Oh. Yeah. That sounds... fancy. Do that."

Crisis averted. Victoria gives you the smallest nod of approval.

choices.text: Signal Victoria for backup
choices.response_text:
You catch Victoria's eye and subtly gesture. She swoops in with practiced elegance.

"Mr. Bryce, allow me to show you our wine cellar selection. We have a rare vintage I think you'd appreciate."

She leads him away, buying time. Smart play - but Jade notices you called for help.

bd_c1_after_dinner.text:
Dinner wraps up around midnight. The guests retreat to the hot tub with yet more champagne. You've lost count of how many bottles they've gone through.

You're clearing plates when Chad calls out: "Hey! New girl! The party's just getting started!"

He's gesturing for you to join them in the hot tub. His friends are laughing, egging him on.

bd_c1_hottub_choice.text: Chad is insisting you join them in the hot tub. This is way outside your job description. What do you do?

choices.text: Politely decline and keep working
choices.response_text:
"I'm flattered, but I'm still on duty! Can I get you anything else to drink?"

Chad shrugs. "Boring." He loses interest immediately and goes back to his friends.

Victoria catches your eye and mouths 'good job.' That felt like a test you just passed.

choices.text: Make a joke and redirect
choices.response_text:
"If I got in there, who would keep the champagne flowing? You'd have to pour your own drinks!"

Chad laughs despite himself. "Fair point. Alright, keep 'em coming."

You've managed to diffuse the situation AND keep him happy. Not bad.

choices.text: Say you'll check if off-duty crew can join
choices.response_text:
"Let me see if any off-duty crew members can join! Derek was saying he's almost done..."

You find Derek, who is MORE than happy to strip down and entertain the guests. Chad's female friend immediately forgets about you.

Creative solution. Victoria looks... impressed? Suspicious? Hard to tell.

choices.text: Slip in - charm is your best weapon
choices.response_text:
You glance around. Victoria's dealing with something in the galley. The coast is clear.

"Well... I AM technically off-duty in about five minutes..."

You slip below deck and change into the bikini you *definitely* didn't pack for exactly this situation. When you climb into the hot tub, Chad's eyes go wide.

"NOW we're talking!" He grins, making room for you. His arm slides around your waist - possessive, but you don't mind. His friends are filming. Let them.

"I like you," Chad says, pulling you closer. The bubbles hide where his hand is resting. "What's your Venmo?"

He tips you $500. Right there. Into YOUR account. Not the crew tip pool.

*This is how the game is played.*

When you finally extract yourself, you catch Jade watching from the upper deck. Her expression is pure murder.

*Good.*

bd_villain_c1_aftermath.text:
By 3am, the party is finally winding down. Chad and his friends are passed out on the sun deck, and you've pocketed your first personal tip of the season.

You catch your reflection in the galley window. Same face, but something's different. Sharper. Hungrier.

*This is who I am now.*

You finish cleaning alone - Jade mysteriously "forgot" to help - and head to the crew mess. Connor is there with wine, sweet as always, but you're already thinking about the next charter.

The next opportunity.

bd_c1_crew_night.text:
By 3am, the promised pool party is in full swing. The guests are wasted, the music is deafening, and you're running on fumes.

Finally, around 4am, they pass out. You finish cleaning and stumble to the crew mess. Connor is there with a bottle of wine and two glasses.

bd_c1_connor_talk.speaker: connor
bd_c1_connor_talk.text:
"Rough first night, huh?" He pours you a glass without asking. "I remember my first charter. Cried in the anchor locker."

He's got kind eyes, this one. And he's looking at you like you're actually a person, not just furniture.

"For what it's worth, you handled Chad pretty well. He's a nightmare."

bd_c1_connor_choice.text: It's late, you're exhausted, and Connor is being surprisingly sweet. Do you:

choices.text: Stay and talk - you need this
choices.response_text:
You sink into the booth across from him and take a long sip of wine.

The two of you talk until dawn - about how you both ended up in yachting, about terrible guests, about dreams of eventually buying your own boat. It's... nice.

When you finally crawl into your bunk, you're smiling.

choices.text: Thank him but get some sleep
choices.response_text:
"That's really sweet, but I'm about to pass out standing up. Rain check?"

Connor's face falls slightly, but he nods. "Yeah, of course. Get some rest."

You catch maybe three hours of sleep before your alarm goes off.

choices.text: Notice Jade watching from the doorway
choices.response_text:
Movement catches your eye - Jade is standing in the doorway, watching. How long has she been there?

"Don't let me interrupt," she says with a sharp smile. "I just came for water."

The moment is broken. Connor mumbles goodnight and leaves. Jade lingers, smirking.

bd_c1_day2.text:
Day two of the charter. The guests are moving slowly - brutal hangovers all around. Chad demands hair of the dog at 9am and complains about the eggs being "too egg-y."

The afternoon excursion goes relatively smoothly. Derek takes them tubing, someone falls off and bruises their ego, everyone laughs.

Then comes the final dinner.

bd_c1_final_dinner.text:
Marco has prepared his signature beef Wellington. The table is set perfectly - candles, crystal, the works.

And then Chad arrives at the table wearing a bathrobe and announces: "Change of plans. We want pizza."

From the galley, you hear something break.

bd_c1_pizza_crisis.text: Marco is seconds away from a meltdown. Chad wants pizza. The Wellington is already done. This is a disaster. What do you do?

choices.text: Get Victoria to handle it
choices.response_text:
You find Victoria and explain the situation. Her eye twitches, but she marches to the table.

"Mr. Worthington, Chef Marco has prepared something truly special tonight. Perhaps pizza as a late-night snack instead?"

Chad considers. "Fine. But it better be good."

The Wellington is served. Chad pronounces it 'acceptable.' Marco doesn't kill anyone.

choices.text: Help Marco improvise gourmet pizza
choices.response_text:
You burst into the galley where Marco is clutching a knife with murder in his eyes.

"Marco! What if we do BOTH? Wellington appetizer, then your signature pizza for the main?"

He stares at you. Then slowly, a mad smile spreads across his face.

"You. I like you."

The hybrid meal is a hit. Chad calls it 'actually creative.'

choices.text: Serve the Wellington anyway, call it 'pizza'
choices.response_text:
In a moment of desperation, you plate the Wellington and announce: "Your deconstructed Italian pizza, sir. Chef Marco's interpretation."

Chad squints at it. "This doesn't look like pizza."

"It's... molecular gastronomy pizza."

He shrugs and eats it. "Weird, but okay."

Marco will either love you or never forgive you. Time will tell.

bd_c1_departure.text:
The next morning, the guests finally disembark. Chad pauses at the gangway.

"Not bad for a first charter. Tell the captain he's got a decent crew."

Coming from Chad, that's practically a standing ovation.

The black SUVs pull away, and the entire crew exhales simultaneously.

bd_c1_tip_meeting.text:
That afternoon, Captain Sterling calls everyone to the bridge for the tip meeting. An envelope sits on the table.

The Captain opens it slowly, building the suspense. He counts the bills.

"Well team... Mr. Worthington left us..."

He pauses dramatically.

bd_c1_tip_reveal.speaker: sterling
bd_c1_tip_reveal.text:
"Fifteen thousand dollars. Plus a note that says 'pretty good for a bunch of randos.'"

The crew cheers. $15,000 split seven ways - plus your accumulated bonuses from good decisions - means a decent chunk of change.

"One charter down, three to go. Get some rest tonight - preference sheet meeting tomorrow at noon."

bd_c1_crew_night_out.text:
That night, the whole crew heads to a beach bar in town. It's the first time you've seen everyone actually relax.

Marco is doing shots with Bree. Victoria is pretending to check emails but you catch her smiling at something Derek said. Even Jade seems less hostile after a few mojitos.

Connor slides onto the barstool next to you.

bd_c1_bar_connor.speaker: connor
bd_c1_bar_connor.text:
"So? Survived your first charter. How do you feel?"

He's standing close - closer than necessary in the crowded bar. His shoulder keeps brushing yours.

Across the room, you notice Derek watching you two. And Jade watching Derek watch you.

bd_c1_bar_choice.text: The drinks are flowing and the tension from the charter is melting away. This feels like a crossroads moment. What do you do?

choices.text: Flirt with Connor - he's sweet
choices.response_text:
You lean into him a little. "I feel like I could use another drink. And better company."

Connor's face lights up. "I can definitely help with both."

You spend the rest of the night talking and laughing. At closing time, he walks you back to the boat. There's an awkward moment at the gangway before he squeezes your hand and says goodnight.

From the shadows on deck, you hear Bree whisper to someone: "Called it."

choices.text: Wander over to Derek - he's been watching
choices.response_text:
You excuse yourself from Connor and drift toward the pool table where Derek is running the table.

"Winner plays me?" you say.

Derek grins that grin. "Stakes?"

"Loser buys shots."

You lose spectacularly. The shots are very strong. The walk back to the boat is... wobbly. Derek's arm around your waist is technically just to keep you steady.

Jade's expression when she sees you two could curdle milk.

choices.text: Join Bree for shots - girl time
choices.response_text:
You slide over to where Bree is holding court with Marco.

"Room for one more?"

Bree grins and waves you in. "Finally! Another girl who knows how to party!"

Three hours later, you know all of Bree's secrets. She knows some of yours. Marco has passed out on the table. The three of you are officially a crew alliance.

You don't remember getting back to the boat, but you wake up with a pounding head and a new best friend.

choices.text: Keep it professional - one drink and bed
choices.response_text:
"Actually, I'm going to call it early. Don't want to be hungover for the next charter."

Connor looks disappointed. Victoria looks approving. Jade looks suspicious, like you're up to something.

You get a full eight hours of sleep and wake up feeling human. While cleaning the crew mess, you overhear Bree telling Jade that you're 'no fun.'

Maybe. But your head doesn't hurt.

bd_c2_briefing_normal.text:
A few days later, the crew gathers for the Charter 2 preference sheet meeting. Victoria looks like she's already developing a stress headache.

"Our primary guest is... Tiffany St. James. Instagram influencer. She's turning 30 and wants the 'most epic birthday ever.'"

bd_c2_briefing_2.speaker: victoria
bd_c2_briefing_2.text:
"She has... let me see... seven food allergies, all developed within the last month. She wants the yacht anchored in 'prettier' spots than our planned itinerary. She wants a photographer to document everything. And—"

Victoria pauses, closes her eyes, takes a breath.

"—she wants a themed party each night. Night one is 'Gatsby Glam,' night two is 'Tropical Paradise.'"

bd_c2_marco_reaction.speaker: marco
bd_c2_marco_reaction.text:
"Seven allergies?!" Marco snatches the sheet. "Gluten. Dairy. Shellfish. Nightshades— NIGHTSHADES? What am I supposed to cook, AIR?!"

"It gets better," Victoria says dryly. "She also wants a 'surprise' birthday cake. With sparklers. Shaped like her face."

The crew exchanges looks of pure dread.

bd_c2_arrival.text:
Tiffany arrives in a hot pink convertible, wearing a rhinestone tiara and followed by three friends who look like they're already exhausted by her.

She poses at the gangway for a full five minutes while her 'content creator' films from every angle.

Then she bursts into tears.

bd_c2_tiffany_cry.speaker: victoria
bd_c2_tiffany_cry.text:
"OH MY GOD, I'm THIRTY!" Tiffany wails. "My twenties are OVER! I'll never be YOUNG again!"

Victoria's smile could crack diamonds. "Ms. St. James, welcome aboard! Thirty is the new twenty, as they say. May I offer you some champagne?"

"Is it low-sugar? I'm also doing keto now. I forgot to mention that on the sheet."

bd_c2_first_drama.text:
The first afternoon is a rollercoaster. Tiffany loves the boat (posts twelve photos), hates the boat (deletes four photos), loves it again (reposts with different filter).

Her friends are exhausted enablers who agree with everything she says. One of them, a woman named Ashley, keeps apologizing to you with her eyes.

Dinner prep begins with Marco screaming about the new keto requirement.

bd_c2_dinner_prep.text:
Victoria pulls you aside before dinner service.

"Tiffany is... delicate. She's already complained twice that the sun loungers aren't positioned right. I need you to be her shadow - anticipate every need before she knows she has it. Can you handle that?"

choices.text: "Absolutely. I've got this."
choices.response_text:
Victoria nods. "Good. Don't make me regret trusting you."

You spend the next three hours memorizing Tiffany's routines, her drink preferences, her phone charging schedule. By dinner, you know her better than her friends do.

choices.text: "Any advice on handling her type?"
choices.response_text:
Victoria's expression softens slightly. "Compliment everything. Agree with everything. And when she gets emotional, mirror her energy. If she's sad, be sympathetic. If she's excited, match it."

She pauses. "Also, her ex-boyfriend might show up. He's been texting. If you see a guy named Tyler arrive, alert me immediately."

choices.text: "That's a lot of pressure..."
choices.response_text:
Victoria's eyes narrow. "This is yachting. There's always pressure. If you can't handle it, tell me now."

You straighten up. "No, I can do it. Sorry. I'm good."

"Prove it."

She walks away. Great. Now you have something to prove.

bd_c2_dinner.text:
Gatsby Glam night. The aft deck is transformed with gold streamers, art deco centerpieces, and enough feathers to outfit a showgirl.

Tiffany appears in a sequined dress, tiara upgraded to a full crown. She's gone from crying to manic excitement.

"This is PERFECT! Oh my GOD, this is SO me!"

Marco's keto-friendly menu arrives. Tiffany takes one look and frowns.

bd_c2_food_complaint.speaker: victoria
bd_c2_food_complaint.text:
"Actually, I don't think I can eat any of this. Can I get something else?"

"Ms. St. James, Chef Marco has accommodated all seven of your allergies plus the keto requirement—"

"But I FEEL like salmon. Is there salmon?"

From the galley: "I WILL BURN THIS BOAT DOWN."

bd_c2_salmon_crisis.text: Marco is at breaking point. Tiffany wants salmon she didn't order. Victoria is frozen. Someone needs to fix this.

choices.text: Check the freezer - maybe there's salmon
choices.response_text:
You sprint to the galley and dig through the freezer. There IS salmon, frozen solid.

"Marco, microwave defrost, quick sear?"

He stares at you like you've spoken heresy. Then he laughs.

"You. Defrost. I cook. GO."

Ten minutes later, Tiffany has her salmon. She pronounces it 'exactly what she needed.'

choices.text: Distract Tiffany with a surprise
choices.response_text:
"Ms. St. James! Before dinner, I have a special birthday surprise - the Captain invited you to the bridge for a champagne toast at sunset!"

Tiffany's eyes go wide. "OH MY GOD, really?!"

You make frantic eye contact with Captain Sterling, who somehow rolls with it.

By the time she returns, she's forgotten about the salmon entirely.

choices.text: Step back and let Victoria handle it
choices.response_text:
This is above your pay grade. You fade into the background and watch Victoria work her magic.

She somehow convinces Tiffany that the beef is 'salmon-adjacent' and that it's actually MORE exclusive. Tiffany buys it.

But Jade notices you didn't step up. "Couldn't handle it, huh?" she whispers as you pass.

bd_c2_night_1_drama.text:
The evening progresses with only minor meltdowns. Tiffany cries twice more (once about aging, once about her Instagram engagement being down), but by midnight she's declared this the 'best birthday ever.'

Then a water taxi pulls up to the yacht.

bd_c2_tyler_arrives.text:
A guy climbs aboard uninvited. He's good-looking in a disheveled, desperate way, clutching flowers.

"TIFFANY! Baby, please! I'm sorry! Take me back!"

Tiffany's face cycles through about six emotions in two seconds. Her friends form a protective circle. Ashley looks at you, panicked.

bd_c2_tyler_choice.text: Tiffany's ex-boyfriend Tyler has crashed the charter. This could go very wrong. What do you do?

choices.text: Get Captain Sterling immediately
choices.response_text:
You race to the bridge. Captain Sterling takes one look at the situation and becomes a wall of authority.

"Sir, you are not a registered guest. You need to leave immediately, or I'll have the coastguard escort you."

Tyler leaves. Tiffany bursts into tears (again) but says you 'saved her' from 'her toxic past.'

choices.text: Step back and let the drama play out
choices.response_text:
This feels like a 'not your circus, not your monkeys' situation. You make yourself scarce while Tiffany and Tyler have a screaming match on the aft deck.

It ends with them making out in the hot tub.

Victoria is furious at the 'security breach.' Captain Sterling is not pleased either.

choices.text: Diplomatically intervene yourself
choices.response_text:
"Sir, I'm going to have to ask you to wait at the dock. This is a private charter, and our primary guest needs to decide if she wants to see you."

Tyler starts to argue, but you stand firm. Security 101: control the situation calmly.

Tiffany sees you handling it and mouths 'thank you.' Tyler is escorted off. You've earned serious respect tonight.

bd_c2_day_2.text:
Day two brings Tropical Paradise theme night. The drama with Tyler seems forgotten - Tiffany is now 'so over' him and focused on 'self-love and my journey.'

She posts forty-seven stories documenting her 'healing process' which mostly involves drinking coconut water and doing yoga poses on the bow.

bd_c2_beach_picnic.text:
The afternoon beach picnic is picture-perfect. Derek sets up a stunning spread on a private beach. Tiffany is so happy she tips him $200 on the spot.

Jade is tasked with serving drinks. You notice her filling Tiffany's glass more generously than usual. By 4pm, Tiffany is very, very drunk.

And she wants to swim. Alone. To 'connect with nature.'

bd_c2_swim_crisis.text: Tiffany is hammered and insisting on swimming alone. Jade isn't stopping her. This is dangerous. What do you do?

choices.text: Offer to swim with her for 'content'
choices.response_text:
"Tiffany! What if we do an underwater photo shoot? I'll swim with you!"

She gasps. "OH MY GOD, YES! Get the photographer!"

You spend the next hour making sure she doesn't drown while pretending to pose for photos. Your swimsuit situation is awkward but she's safe.

Jade looks irritated. Mission accomplished.

choices.text: Alert Derek to watch her
choices.response_text:
You catch Derek's eye and gesture toward Tiffany. He gets it immediately.

"Hey Tiffany, let me show you the best swimming spot! Currents are tricky here."

He swims out with her, keeping her safe while she thinks she's having a spiritual moment. Professional deck work.

choices.text: Confront Jade about over-serving
choices.response_text:
"Jade, you've been pouring heavy all afternoon. She can barely stand."

Jade's smile turns sharp. "And? She's an adult. She asked for full pours."

"She could get hurt."

"Then watch her yourself, hero."

You do. But this confrontation isn't over.

bd_c2_final_night.text:
Tropical Paradise night is a hit. Tiki torches, lei garlands, Marco's (somehow) allergy-free luau menu. The birthday cake shaped like Tiffany's face is disturbing but she loves it.

At midnight, surrounded by sparklers and the sound of the waves, Tiffany makes a speech.

"This was the best birthday ever. You all made me feel so special. I'm definitely coming back."

bd_c2_departure.text:
The next morning, Tiffany hugs each crew member individually. She's crying (happy tears this time) and promising to tag everyone on Instagram.

"Especially you," she says to you. "You really got me, you know?"

The convoy of pink convertibles disappears toward the marina. The crew sighs with relief.

bd_c2_tip_meeting.speaker: sterling
bd_c2_tip_meeting.text:
"Alright, tip meeting. Ms. St. James left us..."

The Captain opens the envelope. His eyebrows rise.

"Eighteen thousand dollars. And a handwritten note saying 'best crew ever, especially the sweet new stew.'"

Jade's jaw tightens. Victoria almost smiles. Connor gives you a subtle fist bump.

bd_c2_crew_night.text:
Two charters down, two to go. The crew celebrates with dinner in town. The restaurant has cheap wine and excellent gossip.

Derek is telling increasingly exaggerated stories about past charters. Bree is trying to get everyone to do tequila shots. Victoria has excused herself to 'check emails' (probably actually drinking alone in peace).

Jade hasn't spoken to you all evening.

bd_c2_jade_confrontation.text:
You're coming back from the bathroom when Jade corners you in the hallway.

"So you think you're special now? Tiffany's new best friend? Victoria's little protégé?"

Her eyes are glassy - she's been drinking more than anyone realized.

bd_c2_jade_choice.text: Jade is clearly looking for a fight. She's drunk and resentful. This could get ugly.

choices.text: Try to defuse - you're not her enemy
choices.response_text:
"Jade, I'm not trying to take anything from you. I'm just trying to do my job. Can we maybe start over?"

She stares at you for a long moment. Something flickers in her expression - almost like she's tired of being angry.

"...Whatever. Just stay out of my way."

It's not friendship. But it's not war either.

choices.text: Stand your ground - you're done being bullied
choices.response_text:
"Jade, I don't know what your problem is with me, but I'm not going anywhere. I earned my place here. Maybe focus on your own job instead of worrying about mine."

Her face twists. "You have NO idea what you just started."

She storms off. You've made an enemy. But you've also stopped being her target.

choices.text: Offer to be her ally - strength in numbers
choices.response_text:
"Jade, look. This job is hard enough without fighting each other. We're both stews. We should have each other's backs. What do you say?"

She wavers. The alcohol is making her more susceptible to emotional appeals.

"...You really mean that?"

"Yeah, I do."

"Fine. But if you screw me over, I'll destroy you."

"Deal."

bd_c3_briefing.text:
Charter three brings a new challenge: Patricia Van Houten and her 'girl gang' - four recently divorced women in their fifties, ready to 'reclaim their youth.'

Victoria reads the preference sheet with growing alarm.

bd_c3_briefing_2.speaker: victoria
bd_c3_briefing_2.text:
"They want... unlimited rosé. A 'hot cabana boy' for beach days - Derek, that's you. A spa day with 'happy endings' - obviously not happening. And they've requested the crew join them for dinner one night because 'we want to feel young again.'"

Derek looks terrified and delighted in equal measure. Marco is muttering about 'drunk women who can't appreciate cuisine.'

bd_c3_arrival.text:
Patricia and her friends arrive already tipsy. They've been drinking in the car. At 11am.

"HELLO BEAUTIFUL PEOPLE!" Patricia bellows as she boards. She's wearing a leopard print caftan and enormous sunglasses. "Where's the ROSÉ?!"

Her friends - Carol, Denise, and Maureen - are slightly more subdued but clearly ready to party.

bd_c3_first_afternoon.text:
The afternoon is chaos. The women want to try every water toy simultaneously. Maureen nearly falls off the jet ski twice. Carol is openly hitting on Derek, who is handling it with increasingly strained professionalism.

By 3pm, they've gone through eight bottles of rosé between them.

Denise corners you by the bar.

bd_c3_denise_talk.speaker: victoria
bd_c3_denise_talk.text:
"You know," Denise slurs, leaning in too close, "I used to be young like you. Then I married a JERK. Three kids and twenty years later, he leaves me for his SECRETARY."

She waves her glass, sloshing wine everywhere.

"Don't make my mistakes, sweetie. Stay single. Stay FREE."

Victoria appears and smoothly redirects Denise toward the hot tub.

bd_c3_dinner_1.text:
Dinner service is... an experience. The women are hammered but charming. Patricia keeps trying to get Marco to come out and accept their compliments on the food.

"WE LOVE YOU, MARCO!" they chant.

Marco, despite his grumpy exterior, is clearly enjoying the attention.

Then Patricia stands up, wobbles, and announces: "Who wants to go SKINNY DIPPING?!"

bd_c3_skinny_dip.text: Four very drunk middle-aged women want to go skinny dipping. At night. This is a safety nightmare. But they're guests. What do you do?

choices.text: Allow it but ensure deck crew supervises
choices.response_text:
You catch Derek's eye and mouth 'safety watch.' He nods and discreetly positions himself with a clear view of the swim platform.

The women have their skinny dip. Nobody drowns. Patricia declares it 'the most liberating moment of her life.'

Derek will need therapy but the guests are happy.

choices.text: Redirect them to the hot tub
choices.response_text:
"Ladies, our hot tub has special mood lighting tonight! Much more romantic than the ocean. And I can bring the rosé TO you..."

Patricia considers. "Ooh, mood lighting? I'm in."

Crisis averted. The hot tub can handle drunk women. The open ocean cannot.

choices.text: Get the Captain to gently shut it down
choices.response_text:
You find Captain Sterling and explain the situation. He appears on deck with practiced authority.

"Ladies, I'm afraid swimming at night isn't safe in these waters. Currents are tricky. How about a nightcap on the bridge with me instead?"

They LOVE this idea. Captain Sterling gives you a grateful nod.

bd_c3_night_1_end.text:
The women finally pass out around 1am. Cleanup is extensive - wine glasses everywhere, discarded clothes in unexpected places, and somehow a sandal in the hot tub.

The crew gathers in the crew mess, exhausted.

bd_c3_crew_debrief.speaker: derek
bd_c3_crew_debrief.text:
"I got pinched," Derek says, stunned. "Like, actually pinched. By Carol. She said I had 'buns like her second husband.'"

Bree is cackling. Even Victoria is fighting a smile.

"Welcome to yachting," she says. "At least they're happy guests."

bd_c3_day_2.text:
Day two starts late - the guests don't emerge until noon, groaning for Bloody Marys. Marco whips up a hungover brunch that they declare 'life-saving.'

The afternoon water activities are gentler. Carol is content to sunbathe while the others do a slow paddleboard tour. Things seem calm.

Then Maureen decides she wants to cliff dive.

bd_c3_cliff_dive.text:
There's a small cliff near where the yacht is anchored. Maybe fifteen feet high. Locals jump off it all the time.

Maureen, still slightly drunk from brunch champagne, is convinced she needs to do this for her 'personal growth journey.'

She's standing on the edge, wavering.

bd_c3_cliff_choice.text: Maureen is about to cliff dive while intoxicated. This could end very badly. Connor is in the tender nearby. What's the play?

choices.text: Signal Connor to position the tender for rescue
choices.response_text:
You catch Connor's attention and point. He immediately understands, moving the tender into rescue position.

Maureen jumps. It's not graceful, but Connor is there in seconds to pull her into the tender, laughing and exhilarated.

"I DID IT!" she screams. "I'M ALIVE!"

Close call, but a success.

choices.text: Swim out and try to talk her down
choices.response_text:
You swim to the cliff and climb up beside her.

"Maureen, how about we do this tomorrow? When you're feeling stronger? I'll jump with you."

She considers, then nods. "Yeah. Yeah, okay. Tomorrow. Together."

You've averted potential disaster. She'll probably forget by tomorrow.

choices.text: Trust she's an adult and let her jump
choices.response_text:
She jumps. For a moment, everything is fine.

Then she surfaces, screaming about her ankle.

The next two hours are spent dealing with a potential sprain, insurance concerns, and a hysterical Patricia. Not your finest moment.

bd_c3_overboard.text:
That evening, the guests want a beach bonfire. Derek sets up a beautiful setup on a private cove. Wine flows. Stories are shared. Patricia gets emotional about her divorce.

And then, as they're heading back to the tender, Denise falls into the water.

Not 'slips.' FALLS. Full wine glass still in hand.

bd_c3_denise_rescue.text:
"MAN OVERBOARD!" Connor yells, already in motion.

Denise surfaces, sputtering. She's laughing, but she's also struggling. The current is stronger than it looks.

Connor dives in without hesitation.

bd_c3_connor_saves.speaker: connor
bd_c3_connor_saves.text:
Connor reaches Denise and hauls her toward the tender. Bree and Derek help pull her aboard. She's coughing but safe.

"My WINE!" Denise wails. "I lost my WINE!"

"I'll get you more wine," you promise, wrapping her in a towel.

"You're my FAVORITE," she declares loudly. "Don't tell the others."

bd_c3_final_dinner.text:
The final dinner is the 'crew joins guests' request. Victoria has deemed it acceptable since it's the last night.

You're seated between Patricia and Maureen. Derek is flanked by Carol on both sides somehow. Even Captain Sterling joins for the first course.

bd_c3_dinner_drama.text:
Partway through dinner, Patricia stands up, glass raised.

"I want to make a toast. To new beginnings. To friendship. And to my EX-HUSBAND, Gerald, who thought I couldn't live without him. LOOK AT ME NOW, GERALD!"

The table cheers. More wine is poured. The night gets messier.

bd_c3_crew_dinner_choice.text: The dinner has devolved into a party. Victoria has loosened up (three glasses of wine). The guests want you to 'really party' with them. You're technically still on duty...

choices.text: Let loose - it's a special occasion
choices.response_text:
You throw caution to the wind. The wine is excellent. The company is surprisingly fun. By midnight, you're doing karaoke with Maureen on the sun deck.

You'll regret this headache tomorrow. But Patricia declares you 'honorary divorced lady' which seems like high praise.

choices.text: Have fun but keep it professional
choices.response_text:
You enjoy the evening but stay sharp. When Denise starts to wobble, you smoothly redirect her to water. When Carol gets handsy with Derek, you create a diversion.

Patricia notices. "You're good at this," she says. "Taking care of people. Don't lose that."

choices.text: Find an excuse to slip away
choices.response_text:
You fake a headache and excuse yourself. But you don't go to bed - you head to the bow, where Connor is sitting alone, looking at the stars.

"Couldn't take any more?" he asks.

"Something like that."

You sit together in comfortable silence until the party winds down.

bd_c3_departure.text:
The next morning is rough for everyone. The guests are a mess. Half the crew is hung over. But Patricia and her gang are glowing with post-vacation bliss.

"This was exactly what we needed," Patricia says at the gangway. "You gave us back our spark."

bd_c3_tip_meeting.speaker: sterling
bd_c3_tip_meeting.text: "Well, the ladies left us..." Captain Sterling pauses for effect. "Twenty thousand dollars. And Patricia wants to book us again next year."

bd_c3_crew_night.text:
The crew night after charter three is subdued. Everyone is exhausted. A quiet dinner, a few drinks, and early to bed.

Except... you notice Jade and Derek disappearing together toward the dock.

Interesting.

bd_c3_jade_derek.text: Jade and Derek are definitely sneaking off together. Their 'history' is apparently present-tense. Do you care? Do you act?

choices.text: Not your business - ignore it
choices.response_text:
Whatever's happening between them, it's not your problem. You head to bed and get actual rest for once.

The next morning, Jade looks smug. Derek looks uncomfortable. Drama for another day.

choices.text: Tell Bree - she loves gossip
choices.response_text:
You find Bree and relay what you saw. Her eyes go wide.

"Oh my god. AGAIN? Those two are toxic. This is going to blow up."

Bree immediately starts scheming. You've either made an ally or started a war.

choices.text: Mention it to Connor - he should know
choices.response_text:
You find Connor and carefully mention what you saw. His expression is hard to read.

"Derek's been all over you and Jade both. Guess Jade's winning."

There's something in his voice. Disappointment? Relief?

"Good to know where everyone stands," he says finally.

bd_c4_briefing.text:
Final charter. Victoria gathers the crew with an unusual expression - almost... relieved?

"Last charter of the season. Mr. and Mrs. Pemberton. Elderly couple, celebrating their 50th wedding anniversary. They want 'quiet elegance.' No parties. No water sports. Just fine dining and sunset cruises."

bd_c4_briefing_2.speaker: marco
bd_c4_briefing_2.text:
Marco is ecstatic. "FINALLY! Guests with TASTE! I will make them the dinner of their LIVES!"

Even Captain Sterling seems pleased. "A nice, calm end to the season. Let's not screw this up."

But Victoria has a warning in her eyes. "They're bringing their adult children. Twins. Bradley and Brittany. Early thirties. Apparently they 'haven't been told about the anniversary trip.'"

bd_c4_arrival.text:
Mr. and Mrs. Pemberton arrive first. They're adorable - he in a captain's hat he probably bought at the airport, she in pearls and a sunhat. They hold hands walking up the gangway.

"Oh Harold, it's beautiful!" Mrs. Pemberton gasps.

"Only the best for you, my dear."

This might actually be nice.

bd_c4_twins_arrive.text:
Then the twins arrive.

Bradley and Brittany Pemberton are everything their parents are not. Designer everything. Matching frowns. Radiating entitlement from fifty feet away.

"Surprise, Mom and Dad!" Brittany says, voice dripping with false cheer. "We decided to crash your little boat trip!"

bd_c4_twins_reaction.text:
Mrs. Pemberton's face freezes. "Oh! Children! What a... surprise!"

Mr. Pemberton looks like he wants to jump overboard.

Bradley is already complaining. "This boat is smaller than I expected. Is there really only ONE hot tub?"

Brittany is on her phone. "The WiFi better not suck. I have calls."

bd_c4_first_dinner.text:
Dinner that night is tense. The Pembertons try to enjoy Marco's beautiful five-course tasting menu. The twins are on their phones, complaining about 'no cell signal' (there is cell signal, they're just dramatic).

Bradley snaps his fingers at you. "Hey. You. More wine. And make it actually good this time."

The bottle you served was a $200 Bordeaux.

bd_c4_bradley_wine.text: Bradley just insulted the wine AND snapped his fingers at you. His parents look mortified. How do you handle this?

choices.text: Kill him with kindness - bring the reserve
choices.response_text:
"Of course, sir. May I suggest our Captain's Reserve? It's usually saved for very special occasions."

You bring out a bottle worth more than Bradley's watch. He has no idea and declares it 'acceptable.' His parents shoot you grateful looks.

Victoria nods approvingly. Class act.

choices.text: Politely educate him on the wine
choices.response_text:
"Sir, this is a 2015 Château Margaux. It's actually quite exceptional. Perhaps if you let it breathe a moment more?"

Bradley blinks. He's been called out, gently. His mother hides a smile behind her napkin.

"Fine. Whatever. Just keep it coming."

choices.text: Signal Victoria - this is her territory
choices.response_text:
You catch Victoria's eye. She swoops in smoothly, handling Bradley with practiced diplomacy. He's still insufferable, but at least you didn't have to deal with him.

Afterward, Victoria says: "Good instincts. Know when to escalate."

bd_c4_night_drama.text:
After the parents retire, the twins reveal their true colors. Bradley wants to throw a party. Brittany is already calling friends to 'come visit the boat.'

"We can get people here by water taxi," Bradley says. "It'll be epic."

"But... your parents wanted quiet," you venture.

"They're asleep. What they don't know won't hurt them."

bd_c4_party_choice.text: The twins want to throw an unauthorized party while their elderly parents sleep. This violates everything the Pembertons requested. What do you do?

choices.text: Alert Captain Sterling immediately
choices.response_text:
You find the Captain and explain the situation. His expression goes from calm to thunderous.

He appears on deck. "No unauthorized guests. No parties. This charter is for your parents' anniversary. Respect that, or I'll call a tender to take you to shore."

The twins are furious. But they back down. The Pembertons' peace is preserved.

choices.text: Try to negotiate a compromise
choices.response_text:
"How about this - I'll set up something special on the aft deck. Music, drinks, just you two. No extra guests, but it'll feel like a party. And your parents can sleep undisturbed."

Bradley considers. "Fine. But make it good."

You set up a private lounge experience. They're satisfied. Disaster averted.

choices.text: Let it happen - they're guests
choices.response_text:
Against your better judgment, you let the party happen. By 2am, there are eight strangers on the yacht. Someone breaks an antique vase. Mrs. Pemberton wakes up crying.

Captain Sterling is FURIOUS. This might be the worst decision of your season.

bd_c4_day_2.text:
The next day, the dynamic is tense. The Pembertons want to enjoy their anniversary. The twins want to sunbathe and complain.

Victoria has you focus on keeping the elder Pembertons happy while she handles the twins. It's delicate work.

bd_c4_anniversary_prep.text:
Mr. Pemberton pulls you aside.

"I know my children are... challenging. But tonight is our 50th anniversary. I want to do something special for Margaret. Can you help me?"

bd_c4_anniversary_choice.text: Mr. Pemberton wants to plan something special for his wife's 50th anniversary. This could be really sweet. What do you suggest?

choices.text: Arrange a private dinner on the bow at sunset
choices.response_text:
You coordinate with Marco and the deck crew. At sunset, a beautifully set table appears on the bow - candles, flowers, their wedding song playing softly.

Mrs. Pemberton cries happy tears. Mr. Pemberton mouths 'thank you' from across the boat.

Even Brittany seems moved, though she's trying to hide it.

choices.text: Suggest the Captain perform a vow renewal
choices.response_text:
"Sir, Captain Sterling can officiate a vow renewal ceremony. We could do it at sunset, just the two of you."

Mr. Pemberton's eyes light up. "Margaret would love that."

The ceremony is simple and beautiful. Mrs. Pemberton can't stop crying. Even the twins put their phones away for it.

choices.text: Create a photo montage of their 50 years together
choices.response_text:
You ask if they brought any photos. Mrs. Pemberton has an album. You work with Bree to create a slideshow set to their wedding song.

Playing it on the main salon screen, the whole family watches together. For the first time, the twins seem almost human.

"This is what we were missing," Bradley says quietly.

bd_c4_final_dinner.text:
The final dinner of the season is Marco's masterpiece. Seven courses of perfection. The Pembertons are glowing. Even the twins have mellowed.

As dessert is served, Mrs. Pemberton takes your hand.

"Thank you, dear. For everything. You made an old woman very happy."

bd_c4_departure.text:
The morning of departure, the whole family lines up at the gangway. Mr. Pemberton shakes everyone's hand. Mrs. Pemberton hugs everyone.

Even Bradley mumbles something that might be 'thanks.' Brittany gives a small wave.

As they drive away, the crew exchanges looks. We did it. Season complete.

bd_c4_tip_meeting.speaker: sterling
bd_c4_tip_meeting.text:
"Final tip meeting of the season." Captain Sterling looks almost proud. "The Pembertons left us... twenty-five thousand dollars. The biggest tip of the season."

The crew cheers. Victoria is smiling. Marco is wiping his eyes (he'll deny it later).

"They also left a note: 'Best crew we've ever had. The new stew is a gem. Keep her.'"

bd_season_wrap.text:
That night, the crew gathers on the aft deck one last time. Tomorrow, everyone goes their separate ways. Some will return next season. Some won't.

Captain Sterling raises his glass.

"To a successful season. To hard work. And to not killing each other."

bd_final_choice.text: The season is over. What matters most to you as you look back?

choices.text: The money - you came here for a reason
choices.response_text:
You count up your share of the tips. It's substantial - enough to pay off some debt, maybe put a down payment on something. You worked hard for this.

"Same time next year?" Derek asks.

"Definitely."

choices.text: The connections - these people became family
choices.response_text:
You look around at the faces you've come to know so well. Victoria, who pushed you to be better. Marco, who screamed but also had your back. The deck crew who made you laugh when things got tough.

"I'm going to miss you idiots," Bree says, voice thick.

choices.text: How much you've grown - you're not the same person
choices.response_text:
You think about the terrified rookie who stepped onto this boat. You've handled drunk guests, crew drama, impossible requests, and came out stronger.

Victoria catches your eye. "You did good this season. Really."

That might be the highest compliment she's ever given.

bd_ending_star.text:
SEASON FINALE

*YACHT STAR*

As the crew disperses the next morning, Victoria pulls you aside.

"I don't say this often. You impressed me. The way you handled guests, adapted under pressure, didn't let the drama derail you..."

She hands you a card. "My contact in Monaco. They're looking for a Second Stew. I recommended you."

Your season tips: [TOTAL_TIPS]

You came in a rookie. You're leaving a rising star.

*THE END*

bd_ending_solid.text:
SEASON FINALE

*SOLID SEASON*

The goodbyes are warm. Hugs, phone numbers exchanged, promises to stay in touch.

"You coming back next year?" Connor asks.

"I think so. Yeah."

Victoria nods as she passes. "See you next season. Don't get too comfortable - I'll expect more."

Your season tips: [TOTAL_TIPS]

Not bad for a first season. Not bad at all.

*THE END*

bd_ending_survived.text:
SEASON FINALE

*BARELY SURVIVED*

The season ends with mixed feelings. Some bridges were burned, some guests were disappointed, but you made it through.

Captain Sterling shakes your hand at the gangway. "You've got potential. But potential isn't enough. Work on it."

Victoria doesn't say goodbye.

Your season tips: [TOTAL_TIPS]

You survived. But surviving isn't the same as thriving. Maybe next season will be better.

*THE END*

bd_ending_rough.text:
SEASON FINALE

*ROUGH EXIT*

The season ends with relief - mostly from everyone else that it's over.

Victoria's feedback is pointed. Captain Sterling's reference letter is... sparse. The tips were there, but the relationships weren't.

"It's a tough industry," Bree says sympathetically. "Not for everyone."

Your season tips: [TOTAL_TIPS]

Maybe yachting wasn't your calling. Or maybe you just need to learn from this and try again somewhere else.

*THE END*

bd_villain_c2_intro.text:
CHARTER 2: MEAN GIRL RISING

You wake to sunlight streaming through your cabin porthole. Your phone shows $500 from Chad - your little secret.

As you head to the crew mess, the temperature drops about twenty degrees. Jade is stirring her coffee with murder in her eyes. Victoria stands with arms crossed. Even Connor won't meet your gaze.

*So. Word got around.*

bd_villain_c2_confrontation.speaker: victoria
bd_villain_c2_confrontation.text:
"We need to talk." Victoria's voice could freeze the Mediterranean. "Chad tipped you separately. You know how that looks?"

"I—"

"I don't want to hear it. What happens in the hot tub stays in the hot tub, apparently. But separate tips? That's a crew issue."

Jade smirks behind her coffee cup. She's loving this.

bd_villain_c2_response.text: Victoria is waiting for an explanation. How do you play this?

choices.text: Feign innocence - you had no idea
choices.response_text:
"I honestly had no idea he was going to do that. He just... sent it. What was I supposed to do, refuse?"

You blink those innocent eyes. Victoria hesitates. Jade's smirk falters.

"Just... don't let it happen again."

*Oh, it's definitely happening again.*

choices.text: Own it - guests tip who they want
choices.response_text:
"Look, I provided excellent service. Chad appreciated it. If the guests want to show their appreciation directly, that's their choice."

Victoria's jaw tightens. Jade looks scandalized. Even Connor shakes his head.

"Wow," Bree mutters. "Bold."

*Damn right.*

bd_villain_c2_sebastian_arrival.text:
The crew briefing is tense, but you barely hear Victoria drone on about the preference sheets. Your mind is already calculating.

Then the guest arrives, and everything changes.

He steps onto the swim platform like he owns it - because men like him own everything. Tall. Dark hair swept back carelessly. Jaw that could cut glass. Tailored linen shirt unbuttoned just enough to hint at the body underneath.

British accent when he speaks: "Sebastian Montgomery. Pleasure to be aboard."

bd_villain_c2_sebastian_look.speaker: sebastian
bd_villain_c2_sebastian_look.text:
His eyes sweep the crew lineup and stop on you. Not a casual glance - a full assessment. His mouth curves.

"And you are?"

Victoria tries to intercept. "This is our third stew, she'll be—"

"I asked her." His voice is silk over steel. Still looking at you.

The crew exchanges glances. Jade's face is thunderous.

*Hello, opportunity.*

bd_villain_c2_sebastian_intro.text: Sebastian Montgomery - tech billionaire, thirty-four, dangerously handsome - is waiting for your answer. The whole crew is watching.

choices.text: Give him your most dazzling smile
choices.response_text:
"[PLAYER_NAME]." You extend your hand. "Welcome aboard. I'll make sure your stay is... unforgettable."

His handshake lingers. His thumb traces your palm.

"I'm counting on it."

Behind you, Victoria makes a strangled sound. Sebastian's female companion - introduced as his "assistant" Natasha - watches with cold, calculating eyes.

*Competition. Interesting.*

choices.text: Stay professional - for now
choices.response_text:
"[PLAYER_NAME], third stew. Whatever you need, I'm here to help."

Professional. Poised. But you hold his gaze a beat too long.

His smile says he noticed. "I'll hold you to that."

Natasha, his "assistant," places a possessive hand on his arm. The gesture screams 'he's mine.'

*We'll see about that.*

bd_villain_c2_cabin_service.text:
That evening, you're delivering Sebastian's cabin amenities when you find him alone. No Natasha. Just him, freshly showered, in nothing but a towel slung low on his hips.

Water droplets trace paths down his chest. His abs are obscene - the kind that come from personal trainers and too much money.

"Ah." He doesn't move to cover himself. "My champagne delivery."

bd_villain_c2_cabin_moment.speaker: sebastian
bd_villain_c2_cabin_moment.text:
"Close the door."

You shouldn't. Every rule says you shouldn't.

You do.

He takes the champagne, pours two glasses. Hands you one. His fingers brush yours - deliberate.

"You're different from the others." His voice is low. Intimate. "You have... ambition. I can always spot it."

"And what do you spot in me?"

"Someone who wants more." He steps closer. You can smell his cologne, feel the heat radiating from his skin. "Am I wrong?"

bd_villain_c2_cabin_choice.text: Sebastian is inches away. The champagne is expensive. The moment is dangerous. What do you do?

choices.text: Close the distance between you
choices.response_text:
You set down your glass. Step forward until there's nothing between you but heat and possibility.

"You're not wrong."

His hand finds your waist. Pulls you against him. The towel is very thin. The kiss, when it comes, is anything but gentle - hungry, demanding, his fingers tangling in your hair.

When you finally break apart, both breathing hard, his eyes are dark with want.

"Tonight. After service. My cabin."

It's not a question.

You straighten your uniform and slip out. Natasha is in the hallway. Her eyes narrow.

*Let her wonder.*

choices.text: Keep him wanting - power is in the chase
choices.response_text:
You take a sip of champagne. Let your eyes travel slowly down his body - taking your time - before meeting his gaze again.

"I don't give anyone what they want that easily." You set down the glass. "But I do like a man who knows what he's after."

His laugh is surprised. Delighted. "You're going to be trouble, aren't you?"

"The best kind."

You slip out before he can respond. Leave him wanting. That's how you keep the upper hand.

*The chase is just beginning.*

bd_villain_c2_jade_sabotage.text:
The next morning, you're setting up breakfast when Victoria storms in.

"The fruit display is wrong. The napkins are folded incorrectly. And WHY is there salt in the sugar bowl?!"

You didn't do any of that. Your setups are perfect.

Across the galley, Jade is polishing silverware with a smile that doesn't reach her eyes.

bd_villain_c2_jade_confront.text: Jade sabotaged your setup. Victoria is furious. How do you handle this?

choices.text: Turn the tables - make Jade look paranoid
choices.response_text:
"That's so strange..." You furrow your brow, all concern. "Jade, didn't you say you were going to 'fix' my setup last night? Something about showing me how it's really done?"

Jade's smile vanishes. "I never said—"

"I just assumed you were being helpful." You turn to Victoria with wide, innocent eyes. "Should I have stopped her?"

Victoria's gaze swings to Jade. "We'll discuss this later."

Jade stares at you with pure hatred. You've just rewritten history in front of a witness.

*Your word against mine. And I'm a better liar.*

choices.text: Confront Jade privately - make it clear she picked the wrong enemy
choices.response_text:
You wait until Victoria leaves, then corner Jade in the laundry room.

"I know what you did."

"Prove it."

"I don't need to prove it." You step closer. "I just need you to know that if you come for me again, I won't play nice. I have Sebastian wrapped around my finger. One word from me, and Victoria gets a preference sheet request that makes your life hell."

Jade's face goes pale. "You wouldn't."

"Try me."

You leave her shaking in the laundry room.

*Message delivered.*

bd_villain_c2_natasha_catches.text:
That night, you slip into Sebastian's master cabin. He's waiting, dressed down in just linen pants, two glasses of wine already poured.

"I was hoping you'd come."

The next hour is... educational. His hands mapping your body. His mouth finding places that make you gasp. The cabin filling with soft sounds and heavy breathing.

You're tangled in his sheets when the door opens.

bd_villain_c2_natasha_scene.speaker: sebastian
bd_villain_c2_natasha_scene.text:
Natasha stands in the doorway, face white with rage.

"You have got to be KIDDING me."

Sebastian doesn't even bother covering up. "Natasha. We've discussed this. We're not exclusive."

"I am your GIRLFRIEND!"

"You're my assistant who sometimes shares my bed." His voice is cold. Dismissive. "There's a difference."

Natasha's eyes find you, venomous. "You're a yacht stew. A SERVANT."

You pull the sheet a little higher and smile your sweetest smile.

"Maybe that's what he likes about me."

bd_villain_c2_natasha_leaves.text:
Natasha is gone by morning - helicopter extraction, per Sebastian's arrangement. The crew watches her dramatic exit from the swim platform with barely concealed glee.

"Good riddance," Bree mutters. "She was awful."

They don't know it was you who pushed her out. They don't need to know.

Sebastian finds you during turndown service, presses a thick envelope into your hands.

"For your... exceptional service. Keep it between us."

bd_villain_c2_tip_envelope.text:
You count it later in your cabin. Two thousand dollars. Cash.

Your personal tips this charter: $2,500. The crew will split maybe $15,000 between seven people.

You're already ahead.

At the tip meeting, Victoria announces the charter tip: $18,000. "Excellent work, everyone."

You smile and nod and pocket your secret envelope.

*This is just the beginning.*

bd_villain_c3_intro.text:
CHARTER 3: THE TENDER INCIDENT

You're prepping for the next charter when Captain Sterling calls a crew meeting. His expression is unreadable.

"We have a... unique situation. A previous guest has requested a return charter. Specifically requested."

Your stomach does a flip. You already know.

"Sebastian Montgomery will be rejoining us. Solo this time."

bd_villain_c3_crew_reaction.text:
The crew's reaction is immediate. Jade's face goes red. Victoria pinches the bridge of her nose. Connor won't look at you.

"A return charter is a compliment to the crew," Sterling says carefully. "But I want to be clear: maintain professional boundaries. All of you."

His eyes land on you for just a beat too long.

Jade's whisper carries: "Wonder who he's really coming back for."

*Let them wonder. Let them burn.*

bd_villain_c3_sebastian_return.speaker: sebastian
bd_villain_c3_sebastian_return.text:
Sebastian arrives with nothing but a carry-on and a smile that's all for you.

"Miss me?"

He says it quietly, passing you on the gangway, close enough that his hand brushes your hip. Victoria definitely sees. Sterling definitely sees.

You don't care.

"Maybe."

His laugh is low and warm. "I arranged a special excursion for tomorrow. Private beach. I'll need someone to... show me around."

bd_villain_c3_tender_plan.text:
The next morning, you're loading the tender with champagne, towels, and a beach picnic when Derek appears.

"I'm supposed to drive you to the beach."

"Actually..." Sebastian emerges in swim trunks that leave very little to imagination. "I'd like to drive myself. [PLAYER_NAME] can show me how."

Derek frowns. "Sir, I really should—"

"I've driven boats before. It'll be fine."

bd_villain_c3_tender_choice.text: Sebastian wants to drive the tender himself. Derek looks uncertain. This is definitely against protocol.

choices.text: What Sebastian wants, Sebastian gets
choices.response_text:
"Derek, I've got this." You flash him a confident smile. "Sebastian is a quick learner. I'll make sure he doesn't scratch the paint."

Derek hesitates, but ultimately steps back. "Fine. But if Sterling asks—"

"He won't."

You help Sebastian into the driver's seat, your hand resting on his thigh as you explain the controls. His attention is... divided.

*This is going to be fun.*

choices.text: Insist on driving - but make it sexy
choices.response_text:
"How about I drive, and you... distract me?"

Sebastian's eyes darken. "Deal."

Derek rolls his eyes but backs off as you take the controls. Sebastian settles behind you, his chest against your back, hands finding your waist.

"Eyes on the water," he murmurs in your ear.

The ride to the beach is... memorable.

bd_villain_c3_beach_trip.text:
The private beach is paradise - white sand, crystal water, not another soul in sight. Sebastian pops champagne while you spread the blanket.

"I could get used to this," he says, pulling you down beside him.

The afternoon passes in a haze of champagne, sun, and stolen moments. His hands. Your skin. The rhythm of waves masking other sounds.

You're half-asleep against his chest when he sits up suddenly.

bd_villain_c3_sebastian_drives.speaker: sebastian
bd_villain_c3_sebastian_drives.text:
"Let me take us back." Sebastian is three glasses of champagne deep, but his eyes are eager. "You showed me the controls. I've got this."

The responsible answer is no.

The answer that keeps him happy is yes.

"Just... take it slow, okay?"

He kisses you hard. "Where's the fun in that?"

bd_villain_c3_the_crash.text:
It happens fast.

Sebastian takes a turn too sharp. There's a grinding crunch - rocks hidden just below the surface. The tender lurches. Water starts pouring in.

"SHIT—"

You're thrown forward as the tender tilts. The champagne cooler goes flying. Sebastian is cursing, trying to reverse, but it's too late.

The tender is sinking.

You're both in the water, swimming for shore, as fifty thousand dollars of yacht equipment disappears beneath the waves.

bd_villain_c3_aftermath_swim.text:
You make it to the beach, gasping. Sebastian is laughing - actually laughing.

"Well. That's a first."

You radio the yacht. Derek's voice crackles back, incredulous. "You WHAT?!"

Twenty minutes later, the backup tender arrives. Derek, Connor, and Captain Sterling himself. Sterling's face is granite.

"Mr. Montgomery. [PLAYER_NAME]." He doesn't say anything else. He doesn't need to.

The ride back is silent. Jade is waiting on the swim platform, smirking. Victoria looks like she's composing your termination letter in her head.

bd_villain_c3_sterling_office.speaker: sterling
bd_villain_c3_sterling_office.text:
"Close the door."

Sterling's office feels smaller than usual. You can hear your heartbeat.

"A fifty-thousand-dollar tender. Gone." His voice is quiet. Dangerous. "Because you let a guest with three glasses of champagne drive. What were you THINKING?"

"Sir, I—"

"You weren't thinking. That's the problem." He leans forward. "I should fire you. Right now. Pack your bags and get off my boat."

Your throat tightens. This is it. You pushed too far.

bd_villain_c3_sebastian_saves.text:
A knock at the door. Sebastian enters without waiting.

"Captain. A word?"

Sterling's jaw tightens. "Mr. Montgomery, this is a crew matter—"

"It's a matter I caused." Sebastian pulls out a checkbook. Writes quickly. Tears off the check and slides it across Sterling's desk.

"One hundred thousand. For the tender, the inconvenience, and to ensure [PLAYER_NAME] keeps her job."

Sterling stares at the check. At Sebastian. Back at the check.

You stay very, very still.

bd_villain_c3_sterling_decides.speaker: sterling
bd_villain_c3_sterling_decides.text:
"This doesn't make it right."

"No," Sebastian agrees. "But it makes it paid for. She stays. That's not negotiable."

The silence stretches. Finally, Sterling pockets the check.

"You're on thin ice." He points at you. "One more incident. ONE. And no amount of money saves you."

You nod. You don't trust your voice.

Sebastian's hand finds your lower back as you leave. Possessive. Triumphant.

The crew is gathered in the galley. They saw everything.

bd_villain_c3_crew_fury.text:
Nobody speaks as you pass.

Jade's glare could melt steel. Victoria won't look at you. Connor shakes his head slowly, disappointed. Even Bree - party girl Bree - seems disgusted.

Only Derek speaks: "Must be nice. Having someone buy your way out of everything."

You should feel ashamed. You should feel guilty.

Instead, you feel... powerful.

*They can hate me. I'm still here.*

bd_villain_c3_party_night.text:
That night, Sebastian decides to celebrate his last evening. Champagne flows. Music pumps. The mood on deck is actually... good? Money solves a lot of problems.

Around midnight, Sebastian pulls you into his cabin.

"I have something special for tonight." He produces a small bag of white powder. "Care to join me?"

bd_villain_c3_party_choice.text: Sebastian is offering you drugs on a yacht. This is spectacularly illegal. The crew is right outside.

choices.text: When in Rome... or Monaco...
choices.response_text:
You've come this far. What's one more line to cross?

The next few hours blur together. Everything is brighter, sharper, more intense. Sebastian's hands on your skin. The music pounding through the walls. Laughing at nothing. Dancing too close.

At 3 AM, you're both on the sun deck, watching the stars spin, when you hear the engines.

A boat is approaching. Official-looking lights.

*Oh no.*

choices.text: Hard pass - you're not THAT reckless
choices.response_text:
"I'll stick with champagne, thanks."

Sebastian shrugs. "More for me."

You watch him disappear into the bathroom. When he emerges, his pupils are dilated, his energy electric. The party continues, wilder than before.

At 3 AM, you're half-asleep on the sun deck when you hear the engines.

A boat is approaching. Official-looking lights.

Sebastian emerges from below, suddenly pale. "We have a problem."

bd_villain_c3_police.text:
Maritime police. Random inspection.

Sebastian grabs your arm, eyes wild. "They cannot find this on the boat. I cannot have this on my record. You understand?"

He presses the bag into your hands. 

"Hide it. Please. I'll make it worth your while."

You have maybe sixty seconds before the police board.

bd_villain_c3_hide_choice.text: Sebastian's drugs are in your hands. The police are boarding. What do you do?

choices.text: Hide it under your mattress - you're in this deep anyway
choices.response_text:
You sprint to the crew quarters. Stuff the bag deep under your mattress. Smooth the sheets. Walk back to the deck just as the officers board.

The search takes an hour. They check everywhere. The galley. The guest cabins. The bridge.

They never check the crew quarters.

"Everything appears in order," the lead officer says finally. "Enjoy your evening."

Sebastian's exhale is audible. His look of gratitude is worth more than money.

*Almost.*

choices.text: Toss it overboard - some risks aren't worth it
choices.response_text:
You walk calmly to the stern. Drop the bag over the rail. Watch it disappear into the dark water.

Sebastian's face when you return is priceless. "What did you—"

"It's gone. You're welcome."

The police search finds nothing. Sebastian is furious but relieved. He can't exactly complain that you destroyed his illegal drugs.

"You owe me," you say sweetly. "Big time."

He knows it.

bd_villain_c3_after_police.text:
The police leave. The yacht exhales.

Sebastian finds you on the crew deck, the stars reflected in the dark water.

"I don't know how to thank you."

"I can think of a few ways."

His kiss is desperate. Grateful. His hands pull you into his cabin. The door closes.

What happens next makes the hot tub incident look like a handshake. Every touch is electric. Every moment stretching. The sheets twisted. Your name on his lips.

Afterward, tangled together, he traces patterns on your skin.

"Come to Monaco with me."

You kiss him instead of answering.

bd_villain_c3_final_tip.speaker: sebastian
bd_villain_c3_final_tip.text:
Sebastian departs the next morning, but not before pressing another envelope into your hands.

"For everything."

Five thousand dollars. Your personal total is now over $7,500.

At the tip meeting, Victoria announces the charter tip: $35,000. "Mr. Montgomery was... extremely generous."

The crew's eyes slide to you. They know. They all know.

But they can't prove anything. And you're richer than all of them.

bd_villain_c4_intro.text:
CHARTER 4: THE TRIUMPH

The final charter arrives: the Harrison family. Old money, conservative values, absolutely nothing like Sebastian.

You almost feel nostalgic for the chaos.

The crew is giving you the cold shoulder. Victoria assigns you to laundry duty - punishment detail. Jade makes pointed comments about 'inappropriate relationships.' Connor doesn't speak to you at all.

*Fine. I don't need their approval. I have their money.*

bd_villain_c4_tip_access.text:
On the last night, Victoria entrusts you with the tip envelope.

"Lock this in the safe. I have to handle the guest departure."

She rushes off. You're alone with the crew's earnings.

$20,000 in cash. Split seven ways, that's about $2,800 each.

Or... you could adjust the math a little. Who would know?

bd_villain_c4_steal_choice.text: You're alone with the tip envelope. $20,000 in cash. Victoria won't be back for at least ten minutes.

choices.text: Take $3,000 - you've earned it more than they have
choices.response_text:
Your hands move before your conscience can catch up. Three thousand dollars into your pocket. The envelope goes in the safe.

When the crew splits the remaining $17,000, they'll each get about $2,400 instead of $2,800. A few hundred each. They'll assume it was a smaller tip.

No one will know.

Your heart is pounding. But your wallet is full.

*This is who I am now.*

choices.text: Pocket nothing - there are lines you won't cross
choices.response_text:
You stare at the money. Count it. Put it back.

Stealing from the crew is different from accepting gifts from guests. This would make you a thief.

You lock the safe and walk away.

Maybe there's a line after all.

bd_villain_c4_jade_suspects.text:
The tip meeting is tense. Victoria counts out the shares.

"$2,428 each. Great work, everyone."

Jade frowns. "That seems low for a $20k tip..."

"It was $17k," Victoria says. "The Harrisons aren't as generous as Mr. Montgomery."

Jade's eyes find yours. She knows. She can't prove it, but she knows.

After the meeting, she corners you in the laundry room.

bd_villain_c4_jade_confrontation.speaker: jade
bd_villain_c4_jade_confrontation.text:
"I know you took it."

"Took what?"

"Don't play dumb." Jade is shaking. "The tips. You skimmed. I saw Mrs. Harrison write the check - she told Victoria it was twenty thousand."

Your heart rate spikes. But your face stays calm.

"Sounds like you miscounted somewhere, Jade."

bd_villain_c4_confrontation_choice.text: Jade is accusing you of stealing. She's right, but she can't prove it. How do you handle this?

choices.text: Make her doubt herself - gaslight her again
choices.response_text:
"Jade." You let concern creep into your voice. "Are you okay? First the breakfast thing, now this..."

"The breakfast thing YOU framed me for—"

"I'm just worried about you. The stress of the season, and now you're making accusations with no evidence..." You sigh sadly. "Maybe you should talk to someone?"

"I— you—" Jade is sputtering. 

Victoria appears in the doorway. "Everything okay here?"

"Fine," you say sweetly. "Jade was just feeling a bit overwhelmed."

Jade's protest dies in her throat as Victoria leads her away.

*Too easy.*

choices.text: Threaten her - remind her what you're capable of
choices.response_text:
You step closer. Close enough that Jade backs against the washing machine.

"Even if that were true - which it isn't - what are you going to do? Tell Victoria? Sterling?" You smile. "After everything this season, who do you think they'll believe? The reliable third stew, or the jealous second stew who's been gunning for me since day one?"

Jade's eyes are wide. Scared.

"Think very carefully before you start throwing accusations around. Some of them might bounce back."

You leave her trembling among the dirty linens.

bd_villain_c4_tip_meeting.text:
The final crew gathering is awkward. Victoria gives her end-of-season speech. Sterling thanks everyone for their service.

You tune most of it out, mentally counting your earnings.

Personal tips: $7,500 (or $10,500 if you took from the crew).
Your share of charter tips: approximately $11,000.
Total: somewhere between $18,500 and $21,500.

The best season of anyone's career. And they all hate you for it.

bd_villain_c4_sterling_speech.speaker: sterling
bd_villain_c4_sterling_speech.text:
Captain Sterling raises his glass. "To the crew. Some seasons test us more than others. This one tested... everything."

His eyes land on you. "I believe in second chances. I believe people can learn. I hope everyone here takes the lessons of this season with them."

It's not quite an accusation. But it's close.

Jade scoffs. Connor looks at his shoes. Victoria's smile is brittle.

Only you raise your glass with a genuine smile.

*Lessons learned, Captain. Lessons learned.*

bd_villain_c4_phone_call.text:
You're packing your cabin when your phone rings. Unknown number.

"Hello?"

"Is this [PLAYER_NAME]? This is Shari Levine from Bravo Development."

Your hands go still.

"We've been... following your season with great interest. Your charter with Mr. Montgomery generated quite a bit of social media attention. The tender incident alone has two million views."

bd_villain_c4_bravo_offer.speaker: victoria
bd_villain_c4_bravo_offer.text:
"We'd like to discuss a potential project. A spinoff focused on... let's call it 'yacht life from a different perspective.' Someone who plays by their own rules."

You sit down on your bunk. This is happening.

"We think you could be that someone. Would you be interested in coming to LA for a meeting?"

The crew hates you. The industry will probably blacklist you. But Bravo is calling.

*Sometimes the villain wins.*

bd_villain_ending_triumph.text:
SEASON FINALE

*VILLAIN TRIUMPH*

Three months later, you're in a corner office at 30 Rock, signing contracts.

'Yacht Queen' - your own show. Six episodes guaranteed, option for more. You'll be the anti-hero America loves to hate. The yacht stew who broke all the rules and came out on top.

Sebastian texts from Monaco: 'Congratulations. Knew you were special.'

Victoria's name pops up in a gossip article: 'Former Chief Stew calls new Bravo star a disgrace to the industry.'

You screenshot it. Frame it. Hang it in your new apartment.

Your season tips (official): [TOTAL_TIPS]
Your ACTUAL earnings: Let's just say significantly more.

The crew despises you. The industry is scandalized. Your Instagram just hit 500k followers.

*Sometimes the villain wins.*

*THE END*

bd_villain_ending_wwhl.text:
SEASON FINALE

*WATCH WHAT HAPPENS*

Six months later. Andy Cohen's living room. The entire crew reunited for the Below Deck reunion special.

Victoria won't look at you. Jade has been giving interviews about your 'toxic behavior.' Even sweet Connor called you 'disappointing' in his podcast.

But you're the one Andy keeps turning to. You're the one with the viral moments.

"So." Andy leans forward, that glint in his eye. "The fans are DYING to know. What really happened between you and Sebastian Montgomery?"

The crew tenses. Jade rolls her eyes. Victoria braces herself.

You take a sip of your drink. Let the moment stretch.

"Well, Andy..." You smile. "I guess you could say something did happen."

Pause.

"Something that's made me very happy. And also about four months along."

The gasp is audible. Jade drops her wine. Victoria's jaw actually drops. Somewhere, Sebastian's lawyers are probably already calling.

Andy Cohen looks like Christmas came early.

Your season tips: [TOTAL_TIPS]
Your future: Complicated. But never boring.

*Watch What Happens, indeed.*

*THE END*
